title: iPhone 18 Pro Aperture Control Goes Fully Manual in Halide 3.2
summary:
**Core Story / Main Event**
* Halide Mark III has released version 3.2, which introduces dedicated support for the iPhone 18 Pro, specifically expanding user control over the device's new variable aperture camera system.

**Important Names, Companies, and Brands**
* Halide (App developer/Product)
* Apple (Hardware manufacturer)
* MacRumors.com (Source of the article)

**Complete List of Products/Features**
* **iPhone 18 Pro Variable Aperture Support:**
    * **Stock App Limitation:** Apple's native app limits users to a four-stop variable aperture (range: ƒ/1.48 to ƒ/4.0).
    * **Stock App Performance:** Provides approximately 50% better low-light performance and increased optical control over depth of field.
    * **Halide 3.2 Enhancement:** Removes the four-stop limitation, allowing users to select any ƒ-stop setting within the camera's full range.
* **Aperture Control Modes:**
    * **Aperture Priority Mode:** User sets the ƒ-stop; the app automatically manages shutter speed and ISO for proper exposure.
    * **Manual Mode:** Provides full manual control over all three settings (Aperture, Shutter Speed, and ISO).
    * **ISO Control:** Halide 3.2 offers manual ISO control, a feature absent from Apple's stock Camera app.
* **Future Feature Consideration:**
    * **f-stop presets:** Currently being considered for future updates based on user feedback.
* **New Film Simulations (Photographic Looks):**
    * **Dawn:** Characterized by filmic warmth in mid-tones and highlights, rich yet gentle shadows, and subtle complementary cool colors.
    * **Quicksilver:** A high-contrast, muted color look simulating a "silver-retention alternative process"; described as a midpoint between color and stark black-and-white.
* **New Framing Option:**
    * **16:9 Aspect Ratio:** A new shooting mode for wider framing.

**Pricing and Availability**

* **One-time Purchase Price:** $69.99.

title: PSA: Apple Mail on Mac May Stop Syncing Microsoft 365 Accounts Today
summary:
**Core Story / Main Event**
* Microsoft has begun disabling Exchange Web Services (EWS) by default in Exchange Online.
* This action disrupts the synchronization protocol used by Apple Mail and Calendar apps on Mac for Microsoft 365 work accounts.
* The transition is part of a "phased rollout," meaning some users will lose access before others.
* Apple is working to migrate Mac apps to the Microsoft Graph API, but the necessary software update has not yet been released.

**Important Names, Companies, and Brands**
* Microsoft
* Apple
* MacRumors.com (Source)
* Jonathan (Contributor)

**Products, Features, and Technical Specifications**
* **Exchange Web Services (EWS):**
    * The legacy protocol used by Apple Mail and Calendar on Mac.
    * New feature development ceased in 2018.
    * Being disabled by default in Exchange Online starting now.
    * Permanent shutdown date: April 1, 2027 (no extensions planned).
* **Microsoft Graph API:**
    * The newer API Apple is working to implement for Mac apps.
    * Intended to support: Mail, Calendar, Contacts, Notes, and Reminders.
* **macOS 27:**
    * The version where Graph API support is expected.
    * Note: macOS 27.1 betas were skipped entirely.
    * Note: macOS 27.2 betas currently contain no mention of Graph support.
* **Exchange Active Sync:**
    * The protocol used by iPhone and iPad (these devices remain unaffected).
* **Microsoft Outlook App:**
    * Suggested Graph-compatible client for affected Mac users.
* **Exchange Online (Cloud-hosted):**
    * The only server environment affected by this change.
* **On-Premise Exchange Servers:**
    * Companies running their own servers are not affected.

**Key Dates and Timelines**
* **2018:** Microsoft stopped adding new features to EWS.
* **2023:** Microsoft announced the start of EWS disabling in Exchange Online (originally targeted for October 2026).
* **June (Recent):** Microsoft updated posts describing the change as a "phased rollout."
* **Today:** Default disabling of EWS begins.
* **April 1, 2027:** Permanent shutdown of EWS in Exchange Online.

**Direct Quotes**
* Microsoft described the change as a "phased rollout."
* Apple states it is "actively working with Microsoft" to move its Mac apps to the Microsoft Graph API.

title: An AI “mind-reading” tool can reconstruct what you’re looking at from a brain scan
summary:
### **Core Story / Main Event**
Researchers at the Weizmann Institute of Science have developed a high-precision AI tool capable of reconstructing images a person is looking at by analyzing their functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) brain scans. The system utilizes a dual-branch "encoder-decoder" architecture to predict both the structure and content of visual stimuli, significantly outperforming previous models in accuracy and calibration speed.

### **Important Names, Companies, and Key People**
*   **Michal Irani:** Computer scientist and lead developer of the tool at the Weizmann Institute of Science.
*   **Weizmann Institute of Science:** Research institution in Rehovot, Israel, where the tool was developed.
*   **Judy Illes:** Neuroethicist and professor of neurology at the University of British Columbia, Canada.
*   **Tommy Sprague:** Neuroscientist at the University of California, Santa Barbara.
*   **Marcello Ienca:** Neuroscientist and philosopher at the Technical University of Munich, Germany.

### **Technical Specifications & Features**
*   **The "Brain Decoder" (Two-Branch System):**
    *   **Branch 1 (Structure):** Predicts the structural layout of the image (e.g., placement of colors).
    *   **Branch 2 (Content):** Predicts the specific subject matter (e.g., "bananas on a plate").
*   **The "Universal Brain Encoder":**
    *   A complementary model that predicts brain activity based on a provided image.
    *   Used in a feedback loop with the decoder to improve both tools via repeated training.
*   **Diffusion Model Integration:** The system uses a diffusion model (AI known for cleaning "noisy pixels") to generate the final high-accuracy image representation.
*   **Data & Training:**
    *   **Initial Dataset:** Trained on data from 8 people who viewed ~9,000 images each.
    *   **Synthetic Data:** Approximately 70% of training data consists of images not originally paired with fMRI scans (generated via the encoder).
    *   **Resolution:** Utilized high-resolution scanners where each voxel covers ~1 cubic millimeter of neurons (compared to standard scanners at 3 cubic millimeters/16,000 neurons).
*   **Key Performance Metrics:**
    *   **Calibration Time:** Requires only **1 hour** of fMRI data for a new user (previous tools required ~40 hours).
    *   **Universal Application:** Can identify shared brain regions across individuals (e.g., specific regions for "food" or "sports").

### **Financials & Release Details**
*   **fMRI Cost:** Estimated at **$600 to $1,000 per hour**.
*   **Presentation:** The findings were presented at the **Cognitive Computational Neuroscience conference** in New York (last month).

### **Future Applications & Risks**
*   **Intended Uses:**
    *   Communication tools for "locked-in" (completely paralyzed) patients.
    *   Reconstructing the content of dreams.
    *   Analyzing PTSD flashbacks.
    *   Expanding reconstruction to video and audio.
*   **Ethical Concerns/Risks:**
    *   **Mental Privacy:** Potential for surreptitious extraction of inner thoughts/mental imagery without consent.
    *   **Hardware Shift:** Transition from fMRI to **EEG** (electrodes/headphones) would make the technology more portable and easier to deploy without a subject's knowledge.
    *   **Legal/Commercial Misuse:** Potential for mental reconstructions to be used as legal evidence or for problematic commercial purposes.

### **Direct Quotes**
*   **Judy Illes:** “The idea [of using this approach] to help people with neurologic conditions … therapeutically is tremendously exciting.”
*   **Tommy Sprague:** “But if there’s a way to surreptitiously extract information about what you’re thinking about, then …150 years of sci-fi can come true anytime, and that’s worrisome in a lot of ways.”

title: How smaller, distributed batteries could help the grid
summary:
**Core Story / Main Event**
*   Startups are bypassing the regulatory hurdles and community pushback associated with large-scale, centralized energy storage in dense urban areas (like New York City) by deploying smaller, distributed batteries integrated into consumer products.
*   These distributed batteries provide immediate benefits to users (cost savings, pollution reduction, resilience) while creating a massive, aggregate power capacity that can be tapped to support the grid during high-stress periods.

**Important Names, Companies, and Key People**
*   **David Hammer:** Cofounder of Pop Wheels.
*   **Pop Wheels:** Company specializing in battery-swapping systems for e-bikes and food carts.
*   **Sam Calisch:** Cofounder and CEO of Copper.
*   **Copper:** Company building induction stoves with integrated batteries.
*   **Every Electric:** Company selling plug-in batteries for homes and businesses.
*   **James Mc Ginniss:** Cofounder and CEO of David Energy.
*   **David Energy:** Company selling plug-in batteries for businesses.

**Complete List of Products/Features**
*   **Pop Wheels Battery-Swapping System**
    *   **Functionality:** Delivery drivers swap depleted batteries for fresh ones at cabinets to avoid charging downtime.
    *   **Scale:** Approximately 50 cabinets across NYC; approximately 2,500 batteries in circulation.
    *   **Food Cart Application:** Batteries used to replace gas generators.
    *   **Specification:** Four batteries can supply five kilowatt-hours of electricity (sufficient for roughly one day of operation for many carts).
*   **Copper Induction Stoves**
    *   **Functionality:** Induction stoves with integrated batteries.
    *   **Key Benefits:** Allows cooking during power outages; reduces the need for expensive electrical upgrades by providing supplemental power during use.
*   **Every Electric Plug-in Batteries**
    *   **Functionality:** Batteries designed to be plugged into air-conditioning units.
    *   **Business Model:** Company provides batteries and pays customers to reduce energy use during high-stress grid periods.
*   **David Energy Plug-in Batteries**
    *   **Functionality:** Plug-in batteries for commercial entities.
    *   **Target Markets:** Laundromats, parking garages, and gyms.
    *   **Business Model:** Similar to Every Electric (incentivizing reduced use during peak times).
*   **Balcony Solar (Comparative Model)**
    *   **Functionality:** Small plug-in modules used to offset home or business energy demand.

**Financial Numbers and Technical Data**
*   **Pop Wheels Capacity:** 5 kWh provided by four batteries for food carts.
*   **Potential Grid Impact:** If every stove in America had a battery, it would add "tens of gigawatts" of power to the grid.
*   **Event Date:** New York Climate Week event on September 24.

**Direct Quotes**
*   **David Hammer:** “The number-one challenge that large-scale centralized energy storage providers have is the fact that their benefits are abstract and their costs are concrete.”
*   **Sam Calisch:** “We’re not just selling a battery for resilience—we’re selling it for cost savings.”
*   **James Mc Ginniss:** “This is the biggest thing to happen in the power grid sector in the last 20 years.”

title: Productive, Durable, Fungible: How NVIDIA AI Factories Maximize Return on Investment
summary:
### **Core Story / Main Event**
NVIDIA is positioning its "AI Factories" as high-ROI infrastructure investments by focusing on three engineering pillars: **Productivity** (maximizing throughput/minimizing cost), **Durability** (extending the earning life of hardware), and **Fungibility** (the ability to run diverse AI and non-AI workloads). The goal is to ensure that massive capital expenditures (measured in megawatts/gigawatts) result in sustainable revenue through high utilization and long-term hardware value.

### **Important Names, Companies, and Brands**
*   **NVIDIA:** Primary technology provider.
*   **Jensen Huang:** Founder and CEO of NVIDIA.
*   **Semi Analysis Agent X:** Data source for throughput and cost analysis.
*   **Sprout:** Source of the September 2026 analysis "The Productive Life of a Data Center GPU."
*   **Barkr:** Source for hardware useful life and resale value data.
*   **Silicon Data:** Source for GPU resale value tracking.
*   **Ornn Data:** Source for GPU rental contract pricing.
*   **CoreWeave:** AI infrastructure operator.
*   **Microsoft:** Mentioned regarding V100 fleet longevity.
*   **Customer Entities:**
    *   Lilly
    *   Pinterest
    *   Revolut
    *   Runway
    *   Texas A&M University
    *   Dassault Systèmes
    *   Wichita State
    *   Lucid Motors
    *   Unilever

### **Complete List of Products, Features, and Specifications**

**Hardware Systems & GPUs**
*   **NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72:** 
    *   Delivers >30x higher throughput per megawatt than GB300 NVL72.
    *   Up to 45x lower cost per million tokens on the Deep Seek V4 Pro model.
*   **NVIDIA GB300 NVL72:** 
    *   Estimated useful life of 9 to 10 years (per Barkr).
*   **NVIDIA H100 System (8-GPU):** 
    *   Estimated useful life of 5 to 6 years (per Barkr).
*   **NVIDIA A100 GPU:** 
    *   Shipped in 2020; still in commercial service 6 years later.
    *   Resale value after 6 years is approximately 25% of original cost.
    *   Rental market pays 80% as much for a 5-year contract as a 1-month contract.
*   **NVIDIA V100:** 
    *   Microsoft fleet ran for 8.4 years (exceeding 6-year book life).
*   **NVIDIA Blackwell:** Used for serving world models (Runway) and vision language models (Pinterest).
*   **NVIDIA Hopper:** Used for training world models (Runway) and vision language models (Pinterest).
*   **Tensor Cores & Transformer Engine:** AI-optimized hardware integrated into a programmable architecture for simultaneous specialization and flexibility.

**Software & Platforms**
*   **CUDA:** The foundational software platform for programming NVIDIA GPUs; ensures cross-generational compatibility so older hardware is not "stranded."
*   **CUDA-X Libraries:** 
    *   Over 1,000 ready-made libraries.
    *   Capabilities: Deep neural networks, computational lithography, quantum circuit simulation, vector search, and climate modeling.
    *   User base: 10 million+ developers.
*   **NVIDIA cuDF:** Used by Revolut for processing billions of transaction records.

**Customer Use-Case Implementations**
*   **Lilly:** 1,016-GPU on-premises cluster for protein, small-molecule, and genomics models, plus chatbots/agentic workflows.
*   **Pinterest:** 14,000 GPUs (Blackwell, Hopper, and earlier) for post-training and deploying vision language models.
*   **Revolut:** Data processing via cuDF and foundation model training/deployment on AI cloud.
*   **Runway:** Training world models on Hopper; serving on Blackwell.
*   **Texas A&M University:** Molecular simulation and AI drug discovery; 95-98% utilization across 26 projects/7 institutions.
*   **Dassault Systèmes:** Virtual twin simulation for aircraft certification (Wichita State) and vehicle design (Lucid Motors).
*   **Unilever:** Digital twin product imagery (reduced production costs by 50%).

### **Financial Numbers, Pricing, and Dates**
*   **AI Factory Cost:** Roughly $60 million per megawatt.
*   **Hardware Lifespans:**
    *   A100: 6+ years of commercial service.
    *   V100 (Microsoft): 8.4 years.

title: The eternal complement
summary:
### Analysis of "The Eternal Complement"

**Core Story / Main Event**
The text is a philosophical and economic exploration of the relationship between "frontier intelligence" (genius/insight) and "institutional intelligence" (execution/capacity). The authors argue that progress is not driven by brilliance alone, but by the "complements" (infrastructure, bureaucracy, and labor) that allow ideas to be realized. The central thesis examines how AI will impact this balance—either by reducing the cost of execution or by creating a "bottleneck" where the volume of AI-generated ideas far exceeds the physical world's capacity to test them.

**Important Names, Companies, and Key People**
*   **Hemanth Asirvatham & Elliott Mokski:** Authors of the essay.
*   **OpenAI:** The platform hosting the series (though the authors note the views are their own).
*   **Nick Bloom:** Researcher who studied research productivity across the American economy.
*   **Galileo:** Cited as an example of low-complexity execution (small telescope).
*   **Einstein:** Cited as an example of intelligence that can substitute for empirical data (relativity).

**Key Concepts & Theoretical Frameworks**
*   **Civilization of Depth:** A potential future where superintelligence minimizes the need for physical capital and bureaucracy through extreme efficiency, hyper-realistic simulations, and precise reasoning.
*   **Civilization of Width:** A potential future where the complexity of nature requires increasingly elaborate, large-scale physical experiments and global infrastructure to make progress.
*   **Institutional Intelligence:** The "uncelebrated" intelligence of execution (laws, funding, supply chains, bureaucracy) required to turn a design into a monument.
*   **Complements:** An economic term where the increase of one input (e.g., a better telescope) increases the value of another (e.g., a better astronomical question).

**Detailed Data & Specifications**
*   **The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST):**
    *   Cost: Ten billion dollars.
    *   Technical Spec: 18 mirror segments engineered to 50 nanometer precision.
    *   Scale: Born from 300 organizations across 14 countries.
*   **Research Productivity Statistics (via Nick Bloom):**
    *   **Moore’s Law:** Now requires >18x more researchers than in the early 1970s.
    *   **Research Effort:** Rose 23-fold since the 1930s.
    *   **Research Productivity:** Fell by a factor of 41.
    *   **Workforce Trends:** Technician workforce is growing 2x faster than scientists.
    *   **Equipment:** Use of specialized equipment in science has doubled over 40 years.
    *   **Chip Fabrication:** A modern chip fab is 5x more costly and sprawling than 30 years ago.

**Modes of Intelligence Advancement**
1.  **Reasoning from Principles:** Pure thought (e.g., Mathematics); replaces search with directed reasoning.
2.  **Insights from Existing Evidence:** Analyzing existing data (astronomical imagery, archives) to find new answers without new data collection.
3.  **Gathering New Evidence:** Intervening in the physical world; limited by physical laws (chemical reaction times, organism growth, cosmic speed limits).

**Direct Quotes**
*   "Genius designs the monument; institutions lay the stone."
*   "The scarce input moves from execution towards taste—the ability to decide what is worth making, which question is worth asking, and which of a thousand plausible directions deserves to be pursued."

title: How Albertsons Companies is reimagining retail from the inside out
summary:
**Core Story**
Albertsons Cos. is expanding its strategic partnership with OpenAI to integrate generative AI across its entire retail operation. The initiative focuses on two primary fronts: enhancing the customer shopping experience (specifically through a new integration with ChatGPT) and optimizing internal business workflows and decision-making for employees.

**Important Names, Companies, and Brands**
*   **Companies:** Albertsons Cos., OpenAI.
*   **Retail Brands under Albertsons Cos.:** 
    *   Albertsons®
    *   Safeway®
    *   Vons®
    *   Jewel-Osco®
    *   Shaw’s®
    *   ACME®
    *   Tom Thumb®
*   **Key Person:** Jill Pavlovich, SVP, Digital Customer Experience at Albertsons Companies.
*   **Third-Party Data Source:** dunnhumby (referenced via the February 2026 United States Consumer Trends Tracker).

**Complete List of AI Products, Features, and Applications**
*   **Safeway Experience in ChatGPT:**
    *   **Functionality:** Allows shoppers to move from a dinner idea to checkout within the ChatGPT interface.
    *   **Input Methods:** Users can start with recipes, photos, digital lists, or simple text requests (e.g., “Plan pizza night for four,” “Put together a quick dinner from the deli,” or “Restock breakfast foods and snacks using store brands”).
    *   **Core Capabilities:** Surfaces relevant products and savings, assists in building a shopping cart, and directs customers to Safeway for final checkout.
    *   **Expansion Plan:** Planned to grow beyond Safeway to include Albertsons, Vons, Jewel-Osco, Shaw’s, ACME, and Tom Thumb.
*   **ChatGPT Enterprise:**
    *   **Functionality:** Deployed to select internal teams to streamline workflows, improve decision-making, and accelerate the movement of ideas into production.
    *   **Target Users:** Teams building retail technology and various business functions.
*   **OpenAI API Integrations:**
    *   **Customer-Facing:** Powers personalized assistance for building baskets, repurchasing familiar items, and planning tailored recipes/meals.
    *   **Internal/Merchant-Facing:** Combines predictive models with generative AI to provide "explainable, data-driven recommendations" and promotional insights to help merchants make informed business decisions.
*   **Existing AI Tools (Expanded upon by new initiatives):**
    *   AI shopping assistant.
    *   "Ask AI" capabilities.
*   **Enterprise-wide Solutions:**
    *   Employee tools.
    *   Commerce apps.
    *   Advertising solutions.

**Financials, Scale, and Key Dates**
*   **Date of Announcement:** October 1, 2026.
*   **Store Scale:** More than 2,200 stores.
*   **Customer Reach:** Over 36 million customers served each week.
*   **Market Insight:** Reference to dunnhumby’s February 2026 tracker indicating shoppers are more open to using AI for groceries than other purchase types.

**Direct Quotes**
*   "This is another practical way we are using AI to reduce friction and make everyday shopping easier." — Jill Pavlovich, SVP, Digital Customer Experience at Albertsons Companies.
